summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR89.2 crores with net profit up 78%, but FY26 revenue fell 7% to INR388.3 crores; FY27 guided at INR600-700 crores.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 20% YoY to INR89.2 crores, with EBIT up 35% to INR9.6 crores (10.8% margin) and PAT up 78% to INR6.6 crores. For full FY26, revenue fell 7% to INR388.3 crores as FY25's high-value chaffs and flares emergency orders were not repeated, while EBIT rose 42% to INR69.3 crores (17.8% margin) and PAT rose 61% to INR45.8 crores, helped by one-off other income. Management guided FY27 revenue to INR600-700 crores and EBIT margin to 15-20%, with the order book at a record INR1,569 crores. Execution remains the central concern: raw material shortages (MIL, DRDO alternate materials), the Katepally plant accident, and pending free-issue material from BDL and DRDO all delayed deliveries.

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 FY26 Defense & Space segment revenue

segments.name: Defense (order book)
segments.commentary: INR1,491 crores, about 95% of the INR1,569 crore order book. Q4 Defense & Space revenue was INR67.7 crores, 76% of quarterly revenue.

segments.name: Explosives (order book)
segments.commentary: INR31 crores, about 2% of the order book.

segments.name: Services (O&M, order book)
segments.commentary: INR47 crores, about 3% of the order book. ISRO-linked revenue is about INR18 crores per year with roughly 2.5 years of contract life left, described as broadly constant.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target INR600-700 crores, versus INR388.3 crores in FY26 (about 50-80% growth). Management said FY27 would be 'commensurate' with the prior year's growth and that the target is 'to try our best'.
FY27 EBIT margin expected at 15-20%, versus 17.8% in FY26.
FY27 export revenue expected at about INR200 crores, with domestic about INR500 crores; management said quarterly phasing will vary.
Of the INR430 crore order won in October 2025, about two-thirds is expected to be executed by end-FY27 and one-third in FY28.

Katepally large rocket motor facility: commissioning targeted by September 2026, with production from November 2026. Broader Katepally RDX/HMX expansion may slip to Q3 FY27, with qualification taking 1-2 months more.
Andhra Pradesh 400-acre defense facility: land price still under negotiation; management expects commissioning 1-1.5 years after the price is finalised.
FY27 capex total of about INR32 crores (INR60 crores less INR28 crores spent in FY26), per management's reconfirmation of earlier guidance.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was about INR28 crores. The FY26-27 plan was INR60 crores in total, comprising Katepally expansion and PDK, which the analyst read as INR45 crores and INR15 crores. Management said the PDK flare plant was already productionised in FY25, with mixers, storage and magazines still under construction.
Katepally: the RDX and HMX expansion is ongoing and not complete. A large planetary mixer and balancing equipment are in progress, and some items are expected to be capitalised by end-Q1 FY27.

Katepally rocket motor facility (large motors for ISRO and DRDO strategic systems) was hit by an accident. Equipment is in fabrication and the building is under construction, with commissioning targeted for September 2026.
Peddakandukur flares plant: rebuilt after an accident about 1.5 years ago, recommissioned, and now producing in-house. Import dependence for flare components has reduced.

Odisha: the first land parcel was rejected and the state government is proposing new parcels. Management is in a video conference with Odisha officials. The three-phase plan has its second and third phases 4-5 years out.

Output is about 50 motors per month across LRSAM, MRSAM and Astra (per management's answer on domestic deliveries). About 40 motors were delivered to domestic customers in the current status described.
demand_pricing: Exports are about 54% of the order book and domestic about 46%. Management said export licences are held for most export orders, and that the INR400 crores of export orders still pending are development orders where invoicing follows milestones.
Newly won INR350.23 crore export order (April 2026) for defence products. Management expects an export licence decision in about 3 months.

A INR18.9 crore order received in February 2026 was cancelled in April because an export licence was not granted. Management said licence rejection risk depends on government policy and the destination country.
Domestic BDL and DRDO orders depend on free-issue materials (FIMs) from those agencies; management said these cannot be executed without them.

Management said alternate raw materials for land mines, loitering munitions and medium-calibre ammunition are in DRDO trials. MIL, the high-explosive supplier, could not meet requirements. Management expects approval within 1-2 months.

Pipeline: QRSAM is not included in the estimates. Some chaffs and flares orders are at negotiation stage and some RFPs are pending. Management expects the order book to stay at about INR1,000 crores-plus after current execution.
Other income: management said the Q4 and FY26 increase came from supplier discounts on delayed deliveries, paid in two parts, and that it is non-recurring.

qa_highlights.question: What growth and margin is targeted for FY27 given fewer emergency orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue target INR600-700 crores and EBIT margin 15-20%. Drivers are land mines, drone and loitering munition payloads, and medium-calibre ammunition, where alternate raw materials have been accepted.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the INR500 crore guidance from February missed (about INR390 crores delivered)?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material shortages: MIL could not supply inputs for mines, loitering munitions and flares. Alternate materials are in DRDO trials, with production expected once approved in 1-2 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Katepally capex on track, and when does it finish?
qa_highlights.answer: Some items to be capitalised by end-Q1 FY27. Full completion may slip to Q3 FY27 because plant and product qualification takes another 1-2 months after commissioning.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export/domestic split of the order book, and how much export licence risk exists?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are about 54% and domestic about 46%. Management said licence approval depends on government policy and the country; the INR18.9 crore cancelled order shows the risk.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the pending order book is stuck, and why?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic orders depend on free-issue materials from BDL and DRDO; about 40 motors delivered recently. Development-stage export orders are being executed against milestones.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the INR430 crore October 2025 order will be executed in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Execution has just started. About two-thirds is expected by end-FY27, with one-third in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Jagdalpur O&M contract lost, and is ISRO renewal possible?
qa_highlights.answer: Jagdalpur was lost in bidding because costs had risen. ISRO contract has about 2.5 years left, and renewal will be bid when the RFP is issued.

qa_highlights.question: Are there chances of similar accidents, and what mitigations are in place?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to automation, remote operations and safety control equipment in new plants. The Katepally rocket motor facility is due for commissioning in September 2026.

risks_watch: Execution: FY26 revenue fell 7% and FY27 guidance of INR600-700 crores needs about 50-80% growth. Delivery depends on free-issue material, raw material approvals (DRDO trials) and the Katepally expansion schedule.
Export licence risk: an INR18.9 crore order was cancelled in April 2026 for lack of an export licence, and the INR350 crore export order is awaiting one (expected in about 3 months).
Pending LD (liquidated damages) reversal: about INR30 crores claim pending with MOD, and final flares supply is expected in Q1 FY27.
Other income: FY26 other income of INR42 crores was one-off, which flatters reported PAT and margins. Core margins may be lower than the 17.8% EBIT headline.
Odisha and Andhra Pradesh expansion timelines are uncertain: Odisha phases 2-3 are 4-5 years out, and the Andhra Pradesh land price is still being negotiated.
The ISRO contract (about INR18 crores per year) has about 2.5 years left, and the Jagdalpur O&M contract was lost in bidding.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order book and long-term structure, but cautious on near-term execution. Management repeatedly qualified targets as things it will 'try' to achieve, and gave vague answers on export licence status, the pending order split, and the average unit revenue of domestic motors.
key_quotes: Highest ever order book stands at INR1,569 crores, representing 4.04x of FY26 revenue and providing strong medium-term visibility.
Yes, it is -- we are to be -- yes, targeting INR600 crores to INR700 crores.
Run rate, we think, it is achievable only.
And by -- as I mentioned, by October-November, other things also we'll be doing.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR600-700 crores (about 50-80% over FY26's INR388.3 crores, midpoint ~60%), backed by a record INR1,569 crore order book (4.04x FY26 revenue) and Katepally rocket motor capacity due Sept-Nov 2026, but management said it will "try our best", Katepally RDX/HMX may slip to Q3 FY27, and execution is hampered by raw material (MIL) and free-issue material shortages.
